findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend Approach step 3 / Scope to require the paired docs/adr/.numbers/0092 marker file (mapping 0092 -> 0092-s3-ticket-store-backend.md) and regenerating docs/adr/README.md via scripts/gen_adr_index.py, since the ADR index is generated and CI (scripts/check_adr_numbers.py) enforces the number<->file bijection.
evidence: docs/adr/README.md line 3: '<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_adr_index.py — do not edit by hand. -->'
docs/adr/README.md lines 5-7: 'each ADR owns a marker file in .numbers/ and CI (scripts/check_adr_numbers.py) asserts the bijection.'
docs/adr/.numbers/0091 contents: '0091-llm-review-carry-trivial-rebase.md' (marker maps number to filename)
Plan step 3: 'Follow the format of the existing ADRs (e.g. docs/adr/0091-*); 0092 is the next free number' — names only the prose file, not the marker or index regen.
findings.finding: The plan's premise that adding ADR 0092 is complete by 'follow[ing] the format of the existing ADRs' is refuted by the repo: an ADR is not a standalone markdown file. docs/adr/README.md is GENERATED by scripts/gen_adr_index.py (carries a 'do not edit by hand' banner), and each ADR owns a .numbers/NNNN marker file (e.g. .numbers/0091 -> '0091-llm-review-carry-trivial-rebase.md') whose number<->file bijection is enforced by CI (scripts/check_adr_numbers.py). The plan's Approach step 3 and Scope treat 0092 as a single hand-authored prose file and never mention creating .numbers/0092 or regenerating the index.
findings.location: Approach step 3 / Scope (docs/adr/0092-s3-ticket-store-backend.md); AC line 'docs/adr/0092-... exists, follows the existing ADR format'
scenarios: ADR 0092 lands as a bare markdown file with no .numbers/0092 marker -> scripts/check_adr_numbers.py fails the CI bijection check.
docs/adr/README.md is hand-edited to add 0092 -> the next gen_adr_index.py regeneration erases the edit (or the drift gate fails).
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: 'docs/adr/.numbers/0092 — new marker file (contents: 0092-s3-ticket-store-backend.md)' and 'docs/adr/README.md — regenerate via `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py` (do not hand-edit the generated banner region).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the '60s' stale-lock TTL against git-remote-s3's own source/docs (cite the release/version), or state the TTL generically (e.g. 'the helper's short lock TTL') if the exact value cannot be pinned, so docs/s3-backend.md and ADR 0092 do not publish an unverified external constant.
evidence: Plan text: 'a stale lock self-heals via the helper's 60s TTL auto-steal (a rare, bounded delay — intentionally not lowered)'
tests/integration/s3_doctor_harness.py:14 confirms 'acquire_lock(ref) -> lock key or None (atomic O_EXCL create, TTL steal)' — mechanism exists but no numeric TTL
The 60s matches in src/rebar/_store/lock.py:46,109,686 are rebar's LOCAL flock timeout, not the git-remote-s3 helper's lock TTL
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the TTL-steal surface exists; the specific 60s magnitude is Unverified against the helper's own docs/source
findings.finding: The plan asserts a specific external-library constant — git-remote-s3's '60s TTL auto-steal' for a stale lock — that will be published to operators, but the specific 60-second value is not verified against git-remote-s3's docs/source. The TTL-steal mechanism itself is corroborated by sibling code (s3_doctor_harness.py: 'atomic O_EXCL create, TTL steal'), but the only 60s value found in the repo is rebar's own local flock timeout (src/rebar/_store/lock.py:109 'could not acquire lock after 60s'), which is unrelated to the helper's lock TTL.
findings.location: Approach step 2(e) / AC line: 'the auto-doctor + 60s stale-lock self-heal behavior'
scenarios: An operator reads docs/s3-backend.md, expects the stale-lock delay bounded at 60s, but the helper's actual TTL differs, leading to unexpected wait behavior or an incorrect ADR/runbook rationale for 'not lowering' the TTL

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In s3-backend.md and ADR 0092, reconcile the merge-based auto-doctor rationale with upstream git-remote-s3's per-reference locking (present at the pinned >=0.3.2), which upstream states 'eliminates the race conditions that could previously result in multiple bundles', and re-ground the 'interactive and discards a head' characterization against upstream's actual doctor behavior ('creates a new branch for every bundle that should not be retained').
evidence: Plan claims: 'the non-interactive auto-doctor self-heals a multiple-bundles state by merge (no data loss)' and 'the multi-bundle risk is handled by a rebar merge-based auto-doctor because upstream's git-s3 doctor is interactive and discards a head'

Retrieved upstream README/PyPI (git-remote-s3, incl. 0.3.2 on Libraries.io): 'This locking mechanism eliminates the race conditions that could previously result in multiple bundles per reference, ensuring consistent repository state across concurrent operations.'

Retrieved upstream: doctor 'by default it will create a new branch for every bundle that should not be retained' — i.e. it does not silently discard; the plan's 'interactive and discards a head' framing should be re-grounded against this wording
findings.finding: The plan's motivation for a rebar merge-based auto-doctor rests on the multiple-bundles state, but upstream git-remote-s3 (at the pinned >=0.3.2) now documents per-reference locking that it says 'eliminates the race conditions that could previously result in multiple bundles per reference'; the plan does not reconcile whether its auto-doctor is still needed at that version or is only legacy-state cleanup.
findings.location: Approach step 2(e) and step 3 (ADR rationale); AC line 2 and AC line 3
scenarios: Operator reads s3-backend.md / ADR at git-remote-s3 0.3.2 where per-ref locking is present and questions why a rebar auto-doctor exists
Reviewer of the sibling code story cannot tell whether the auto-doctor addresses a live risk or a pre-locking legacy risk
findings.suggested_fix: State that per-ref locking (>=0.3.2, 60s TTL) is the primary prevention and position the rebar auto-doctor as bounded reconciliation for residual/legacy multiple-bundle states; correct the doctor description to 'creates side branches per bundle rather than merging (non-interactive by default)' per the upstream README.

findings.finding: Neither the operator guide nor the ADR addresses teardown / deletion safety for the stateful, versioned S3 bucket and customer CMK that hold the entire ticket history — the T10 blast-radius/teardown check expects destroy/replace safety for stateful resources.

scenarios: An operator decommissions the S3 backend or scheduling deletion of the CMK, and irrecoverably loses (or renders unreadable) the ticket history because no retention/protection guidance was given.
